Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited 48% figure is from 2016 and badly outdated. World Bank/ITU data (via Trading Economics) shows 71.93% of Gabon's population using the internet in 2023, and DataReportal/Kepios (GSMA Intelligence-sourced) reports 73.7% for 2024 and 71.9% for 2025 — consistently above 70%. Value code changed from 3 (30-49%) to 5 (70%+) on the basis of these corroborating, more recent sources.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited 124-126% figure (DataReportal/GSMA Intelligence, 2025-2026) measures total cellular connections/SIMs, not unique subscribers as the variable strictly requires — multi-SIM ownership inflates this well above 100% and is not a valid proxy on its own. No GSMA Intelligence figure specific to Gabon's unique-subscriber percentage could be located. Given internet usage alone stands at roughly 72% (World Bank/ITU, 2023-2025), unique mobile subscriber penetration is very likely above 70%, so code 5 remains plausible, but confirmation rests on an indirect proxy rather than a direct unique-subscriber statistic — flagged for human review to source GSMA Intelligence's unique-subscriber metric directly.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Law No. 001/2011 enacted with CNPDCP DPA established [Data Protection Africa](https://dataprotection.africa/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Gabon-Factsheet.pdf)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed against the official Journal Officiel text of Loi n°001/2011 (which established the CNPDCP data protection authority) and its 2023 amendment, Loi n°025/2023 (12 July 2023), which replaces CNPDCP with a new authority, the APDPVP, retaining sanction/enforcement powers (Articles 199-204). Legislation is enacted and a DPA exists, supporting code 4; no independent evidence of the 'active enforcement and regional alignment' needed for code 5 was found, so the score is confirmed rather than upgraded, with the 2011/2023 legal basis updated in the sources.

revision_notes: Confirmed directly against the World Bank's own country data page, which lists 94.1% electricity access as the most recent value (2023), matching the cited figure and code 5 (90%+). No fresher (2024/2025) World Bank data point is yet available.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited 2015 figure (51.7% hydro) would actually sit in category 4 (50-74%), not the code 3 assigned, so the original row was internally inconsistent. Fresher data is mixed between sources but both still corroborate category 3: World Bank/IEA data shows renewable electricity output at 31.59% of total generation in 2021, while EIA-sourced data (via TheGlobalEconomy) shows hydropower — Gabon's only material renewable source — at 47.86% of generation in 2023, against 52.11% fossil fuels. Both figures fall within the 25-49% band, so code 3 is confirmed on fresher, more reliable sources despite the flawed original citation.
